test_title: PYST 2: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 29 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Match the financial power/body with its primary function:

 
 

 
 
**List I (Power/Body)**

 
 
 
**List II (Function)**

 
 
 

 
 
1.

 
 Finance Commission
 
 
P.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Finance Commission:** - The Finance Commission is primarily responsible for **tax distribution**. It recommends the division of tax revenues between the Union and the States and among the States themselves. - It plays a crucial role in ensuring fiscal federalism. - Hence, **Finance Commission matches with R.**
 
• **Article 282:** - Article 282 of the Indian Constitution allows the Union or the State governments to provide **discretionary grants** for public purposes. - These grants are not bound by specific constitutional provisions but can be given at the discretion of the government. - Hence, **Article 282 matches with P.**
 
• **Consolidated Fund:** - The Consolidated Fund is the repository of **all Union revenues**, including direct and indirect taxes, non-tax revenues, and borrowings. - It is used for various expenditures, and no money can be withdrawn from it without parliamentary approval. - Hence, **Consolidated Fund matches with S.**
 
• **Contingency Fund:** - The Contingency Fund is used to meet **unexpected expenses** that may arise during emergencies. - It is kept at the disposal of the President and is replenished from the Consolidated Fund. - Hence, **Contingency Fund matches with Q.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Finance Commission (Article 280):**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is appointed every **five years** by the President to recommend financial distributions between the Union and States.
 
• The recommendations include principles for tax distribution and grants-in-aid for States.
 
 
 
• **Article 282:**
 
 
• Article 282 of the Constitution provides discretionary powers to the Union and State governments to allocate grants for **public purposes**.
 
• These grants are not tied to specific constitutional provisions but are offered based on necessity.
 
 
 
• **Consolidated Fund of India:**
 
 
• It is the most significant fund managed by the Indian government and includes **all revenues received by the Union government.**
 
• Expenditures from the Consolidated Fund require prior approval from the **Parliament**.
 
• The fund ensures accountability in financial transactions of the government.
 
 
 
• **Contingency Fund:**
 
 
• It serves as an emergency fund for **unexpected and urgent expenses.**
 
• The fund is maintained under the authority of the **President** and can only be used for unforeseen circumstances.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Finance Commission:** - The Finance Commission ensures equitable financial distribution and strengthens fiscal federalism. - Example: The **15th Finance Commission (2020-25)** recommended tax devolution rates.
 
• **Article 282:** - Discretionary grants under Article 282 are used for specific purposes like disaster relief or special schemes.
 
• **Consolidated Fund:** - It covers regular government expenditures like salaries, infrastructure, and welfare schemes.
 
• **Contingency Fund:** - It is utilized during emergencies like natural disasters or wartime situations. - Example: The **Contingency Fund of India** is maintained at Rs. 500 crores.
